title: Defence by waiting: when it works
outcomes: Holds a good set-up instead of changing it without a reason
Recognises when the opponent has a way forward and waiting stops working
Switches plan at the right moment

steps.text:
**Defence by economy:** when the opponent has no clear way forward, do not change your set-up without a reason. Needless pawn moves, king walks and rook shuffles give him free tempi. Hold the best post you have and make him commit first.
**Rule of thumb** in the middlegame; the ending below is exact.

steps.caption: Black to move. White's pawn cannot advance safely yet.

line.say: Black waits: the rook stays on the sixth rank.

claims.statement: Exact result from the tablebase: a draw.

steps.text: Waiting is right only while the opponent has no way forward. Ask: **can he improve his position by force? If not, keep the best set-up.** If he can, waiting is just passive, and you must change plan. In the next position only the pawn has moved.
